purpose: Extend the existing shared logical-entry hook to snapshot RCX, RDX, and raw [RDX+0x10] together for every seeded external caller, preserve the snapshot through recursive calls, and correlate it with the exact root descriptor.

capture_design.method: single shared logical-entry hook; capture first two x64 argument registers at callee entry and reuse the entry-time [RDX+0x10] read
capture_design.caller_coverage: all runtime callers pass through the shared hook; retains caller return RVA and 52-static-candidate classification; recursive entries inherit the external caller snapshot
capture_design.timing_limit: snapshot is at shared callee entry immediately after the call, before the hooked function body proceeds; it is not a pre-instruction breakpoint snapshot

interpretation.inference: One hook at the shared entry can observe all dynamically reaching caller sites in one run. The x64 argument registers are available as the hook's first two arguments; the [RDX+0x10] value is already sampled there by the current lane probe.
interpretation.hypothesis: For the target indirect dispatch, the callee-entry RCX/RDX snapshot will preserve the relevant call-boundary values; validate this against a live 0.3.37 capture before treating the slot as the resolved dispatch target.
